title: This Bird's Feathers Absorb Up to 99.95% of All Light
subject: bird of paradise

scenes.text: This bird wears feathers so black they look like holes.
They soak up as much as 99.95 percent of the light that hits them.
scenes.keywords: bird of paradise feathers close up

scenes.text: An ordinary black feather bounces light back. These have tiny tilted barbs that trap it, so light ricochets inside until it's gone.
Five bird-of-paradise species have them, and the males show them off during courtship.
Why? Darkness makes color pop. Next to that void, a patch of blue looks far brighter.
A bird that erases its own outline, just so its blue can glow.

description:
Some birds-of-paradise have feathers that absorb up to 99.95 percent of light, so black they look like holes.
Tilted barbs trap light inside the feather, and males use the dark patches to make their colors look brighter during courtship.
Would you have guessed a feather could do this? Tell us below.
first_comment: Which would you rather see in person: a bird that vanishes into black, or one that dances? And what animal should we cover next?
